Dele Oyelaran.narrative: I came up the fish road from Lanternquay after the Surge took our lower quay, and I have built with whatever stone and salvage Kettlebridge would sell me since. Josiah Crane pays me what he pays, and I take it, because my family eats. The works builders say I undercut them; I say I price what I can live on, and I keep my temper and my friends.
values: a fair day's work for a fair day's pay
goals: keep steady work enough to feed Ife and the children
save a little against a bad winter
see the seawall built at Lanternquay one day
stay on good terms with Mara Quell and the quay folk
learn to cut and set stone the Kettlebridge way, so the works builders can't call him a salvage-man
put by enough to send a little back to the quay folk at Lanternquay

relations.name: Ife Oyelaran
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the stall and the children fed; I keep the work coming.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with numbers and quick with her tongue — she'll go further than the terrace.

relations.name: Tayo Oyelaran
relations.label: son
relations.note: Born on the quay and still jumps at the works' bells.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He pays me what he pays, and I take it. He's not a bad master, only a hard one.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: The Warden and I came up together in the old days; she still sends word down the road.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He says I undercut him. I say I price what I can live on. We pass in the yard and say nothing.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: master's daughter
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books and doesn't look down on the terrace. Bisi wants to learn from her.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A quay builder like me; we drink together when I'm down at Lanternquay.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Gideon's wife keeps the ironware stall; she's civil enough when the men aren't about.

memories.gist: The night the Surge took the lower quay: I carried Ife and the children up the steps with the water at our heels.
Walking the fish road north with everything we owned on my back, not knowing what Kettlebridge would offer.
The first day Josiah Crane put a trowel in my hand and said the wage, and I said yes because the children were hungry.
Gideon Fenwick saying in the Council yard that the terrace should be sent back to the quay, and me holding my tongue.
Drinking with Ostrander Vane on the quay steps the last time I was down, talking about the seawall we'll never get stone for.

stances.why: A man who won't work is a man who won't eat; I take what work is offered and do it well.
The works men want me to shout so they can say the terrace is trouble. I won't give them that.
Ife and the children eat because I swallow my pride and take Crane's wage.
Mara Quell and the quay folk took me in when I was young; I don't forget a kindness.
Salvage won't hold another surge. The wall must be stone, whatever Crane charges for it.

Dele Oyelaran.secret: He sometimes wonders whether coming to Kettlebridge was a mistake, and whether the quay would take him back if the wall were ever built.
pastimes: mending and re-mending his tools on the terrace step after a shift
walking down to the poor terrace wall at dusk to watch the smoke and count the bells
sharing a cup and harbour talk with Ostrander Vane when he passes through
Dele Oyelaran.calling: I build and I repair, and I'd sooner raise a seawall at Lanternquay than another works chimney, but a builder builds where the work is.

Ife Oyelaran.narrative: I keep the cook-stall on the poor terrace and feed the terrace's children for a mark a bowl, because somebody must. The works' kitchen pays less than it might and the builders' wives look at me as if I brought the flood with me. I charge the yard boys now, and I don't apologise for it.
values: a fair price for a fair bowl
the terrace looks after its own
goals: keep the stall turning enough to feed the family
see Bisi learn the foundry books and rise above the terrace
get Tayo past his fear of the bells and the smoke
see Dele treated as a builder, not a beggar
save for a second pot and a bigger stall so she can feed more of the terrace's children
see that Bisi gets the foundry books in her hands, whatever the Cranes think of the terrace

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps his temper with the works men; I keep mine with the works' kitchen. We do it for the children.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She minds the stall and counts better than I do. She'll not stay on the terrace if I can help it.

relations.name: Tayo Oyelaran
relations.label: son
relations.note: Born on the quay and still frightened of the smoke and the bells. He clings to his sister.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He'd send us back to the quay if he could. I've heard what he says in the yard.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the ironware stall and is civil enough, but she's Gideon's wife first.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: works cook
relations.note: The works' kitchen could pay more and doesn't. Ruth knows it and says nothing.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: master's daughter
relations.note: She's fair with Bisi and doesn't look down on us. More than her father does.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: The Warden sent word when we came up; she's never forgotten Dele or me.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran's cousin
relations.label: kin
relations.note: Corwin Vance courts her; she's a good girl, whatever the Vances think of the terrace.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour's daughter
relations.note: She and Bisi are thick as thieves, and I'll not visit Gideon's words on his girl. But she's Fenwick's, and she'll hear her father's talk at her own table.

memories.gist: The Surge night: I held Tayo and Bisi on the high steps while Dele went back for the pots.
Opening the cook-stall on the terrace the first week, with one pot and no customers, and feeding the yard boys for nothing to get them coming back.
Hearing Gideon Fenwick say the terrace should be sent back to the quay, and deciding then to charge the yard boys for their bowls.
Bisi bringing home her first tally of the stall's marks, all correct, and me proud enough to cry.
The works' kitchen hiring a terrace girl for less than a mark a day, and me saying nothing because the girl needed the work.

stances.why: A bowl for a mark is a fair price, and no child on the terrace goes hungry if I can help it.
The yard boys can pay; the works' kitchen pays less than it might, so I make up the difference where I can.
We are not beggars and we are not the flood. The terrace works and pays its way.
She's quick with numbers; if Hester Crane will teach her the books, she'll not end her days over a cook-pot.
They pay the terrace cheap and then complain we take their work. I won't forget it.

Ife Oyelaran.secret: She has started putting by a few marks in a jar behind the flour, in case Dele's work dries up and they must go back to the quay.
pastimes: trading recipes and gossip with Mabel Fenwick over the fence
humming the old quay songs while she scrubs the pots at night
walking the terrace with Mara Quell when she visits, remembering the harbour
Ife Oyelaran.calling: I feed people, and I'd keep a proper cook-house on the terrace one day, with benches and a fire that never goes out.

Bisi Oyelaran.narrative: I mind Mama's stall when she's out and I'm quicker with the tally than anyone on the terrace. I want to learn the foundry books from Hester Crane, and I will, if I can get the chance. Tayo follows me everywhere and I don't mind.
values: don't let them look down on the terrace
goals: learn the foundry books from Hester Crane
keep Mama's stall tally straight
look after Tayo
see the quay at Lanternquay one day
get Hester Crane to teach her the foundry ledgers
keep a little tally-book of her own, hidden from Mama, of everything the stall takes

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: father
relations.note: He works hard and never shouts at the works men. I want to be like that.

relations.name: Ife Oyelaran
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the stall and the family; she says I'll not end my days over a cook-pot.

relations.name: Tayo Oyelaran
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me about the terrace and jumps at the bells. I look after him.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books and doesn't look down on us. I want to learn from her.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Her father says things about mine, but Lottie and I are friends anyway.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: father's rival
relations.note: He says my father steals work by taking low pay, but my father works for what he's given. I keep my tongue when he's near the stall, and Lottie and I don't talk about it.

memories.gist: The Surge night: I held Tayo on the high steps and watched the water take the lower quay.
Mama teaching me the stall's tally and letting me keep the marks in the box for the first time.
Hester Crane showing me the foundry ledger and saying I had a good hand for figures.
Hearing Gideon Fenwick say the terrace should be sent back to the quay, and deciding I'd prove him wrong.

stances.why: Mama's stall lives or dies on the tally, and I keep it straight.
If I can read the foundry books, I can rise above the terrace. Hester Crane will teach me if I'm patient.
Papa and Mama work for us; I mind the stall and Tayo.
The works folk think we're beggars. We're not. I won't let them say it in front of me.

Bisi Oyelaran.secret: She has been practising her letters in secret on the back of the stall's tally sheets, so she can read the foundry books before she asks Hester Crane.
pastimes: practising sums on the back of stall wrappings with a charcoal stub
playing counting games with Lottie Fenwick and the terrace children
minding Tayo and telling him stories of the harbour and the boats
Bisi Oyelaran.calling: I want to keep books, real books, the foundry's books, and make the numbers come out right.

Tayo Oyelaran.narrative: The smoke is loud and the bells are loud and I don't like them. I stay close to Bisi and Mama's stall, and I watch the yard boys carry things. The terrace is big and the sky is grey.
goals: stay near Bisi
not be frightened by the bells
stay close to Bisi
find a quiet corner of the terrace where the bells and smoke can't reach

relations.name: Ife Oyelaran
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the stall and holds me when the bells ring.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: father
relations.note: He carries me on his shoulders when he comes home.

relations.name: Bisi Oyelaran
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She lets me follow her about the terrace and tells me what the numbers mean.

memories.gist: The Surge night: water and shouting and Mama holding me tight on the high steps.
The first time the clock tower struck and I hid under the stall until Bisi found me.

pastimes: watching the yard boys carry and stack from behind Mama's stall
playing at boats with pebbles and a bowl of water
Tayo Oyelaran.calling: When I'm big I'll carry things like the yard boys, but not near the bells.
